recognize_zh: 三色染色（trichrome）下，骨髓腔內有大量藍染膠原纖維呈束狀、漩渦狀穿插在造血細胞之間，右上可見紅染骨小樑，代表膠原性纖維化（collagen fibrosis）。
features: Blue-staining collagen bands streaming and swirling through the marrow space on trichrome
Collagen fibers intersect around and separate residual hematopoietic cells
Cellular intertrabecular space with spindled stromal cells
Scattered gray-brown pigmented cells, likely hemosiderin-laden macrophages
Adjacent bony trabecula (red) at upper right; small vessel at lower center
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy, Masson trichrome stain, shows an intertrabecular space extensively replaced by blue-staining collagen bundles arranged in streaming and whorled fascicles. Residual hematopoietic cells and spindled stromal cells are entrapped between the collagen bands, and scattered pigmented macrophages are present. Adjacent trabecular bone is seen at the upper right. Findings are consistent with collagen fibrosis of the marrow (trichrome-positive, corresponding to grade MF-3); correlation with reticulin grading, clinical history and molecular studies is needed to separate reactive from neoplastic causes.

ddx.vs: PMF shows clustered, atypical cloud-like megakaryocytes and osteosclerosis with driver mutations (JAK2/CALR/MPL), whereas reactive fibrosis lacks megakaryocytic atypia.
Metastatic tumor shows cohesive epithelial clusters within the fibrosis that are keratin-positive, not seen here.
Marrow Hodgkin lymphoma shows fibrosis with a mixed inflammatory background containing CD30+/CD15+ Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells.
HCL shows a diffuse reticulin (not collagen) increase with fried-egg lymphoid cells that are CD20+/annexin A1+/BRAF V600E+.
